title: Finite 10 and 14 descendant modules form integrable AdS unfolded toys but carry no local propagation

claim.statement: The corrected SO(2,3) adjoint-10 and symmetric-traceless-14 descendants support exact finite-dimensional covariantly constant AdS4 unfolded systems, but those systems are topological/rigid rather than propagating field theories.
claim.researchConsequence: The programme should retain these modules as kinematic seeds while adding an infinite Weyl module or differential gauge-form sector for genuine local gravity.

setup.unfoldedEquation: D C = (d + omega^{ab} R(J_ab) + e^a R(P_a)) C = 0

interpretation: The immediate descendant maps found in v645 are the component form of a bona fide SO(2,3) representation connection.
The noncommuting AdS translations close onto Lorentz generators, so D^2 vanishes when AdS curvature cancels the vierbein wedge term.
The vector seeds generate every Lorentz descendant in one translation step and are generated back in one step.
Finite-dimensional covariantly constant zero-forms have only finite initial data and no arbitrary local wave data; representation closure alone therefore cannot supply propagating gravitons.
falsifiers: Any failure of the representation commutator [R(P_a),R(P_b)]=R([P_a,P_b]) would invalidate integrability; residuals are below 5e-15.
Local propagation would require solutions with arbitrary functional initial data modulo constraints; the finite parallel-section equation does not provide this.
The no-propagation statement does not exclude dynamics after coupling to gauge forms, interactions, boundaries, or infinite modules.
nextBranches: Construct the minimal SO(2,3) gauge one-form sector and linearized curvature equations around AdS4.
Build the first levels of an infinite Weyl module seeded by the Lorentz symmetric-traceless tensor.
Test whether candidate-48 scalar seeds can source the gauge curvature consistently without violating the residual-U(1) Hessian constraints.
